assets.label: Figure A5.1
assets.caption: Figure A5.1 Some basic geometric concepts of vectors. While we use examples from two dimensions, these concepts easily extend to $n$ dimensions. A: A vector $x$ can be thought of as an arrow from the origin to a point in space whose coordinates are given by the elements of $x$. B: Multiplying a vector by $-1$ results in a reflection about the origin. C: One measure of the difference in direction between two vectors is the angle $(\theta)$ between them. D: Proj($\mathbf{b}$ on $\mathbf{a}$) is the vector resulting from the projection of $\mathbf{b}$ onto a. Note that the resulting projection vector is either in the same direction as $a$ or in the direction of the reflection of $a$, as seen for Proj($\mathbf{c}$ on $\mathbf{a}$).

assets.label: Figure A5.5
assets.caption: Figure A5.5 The general shape of surfaces of constant variance for the additive-genetic covariance matrix, G, given in Example A5.1. Defining a new composite character  $ y = az_1 + bz_2 $, the rotated ellipse represents the set of weights  $ (a, b) $ that give y the same additive-genetic variance,  $ c^2 $. The major axis of the ellipse is along  $ e_2 $, the eigenvector associated with the smallest eigenvalue of G, where  $ \lambda_2 \simeq 0.765 $, giving  $ 1/\sqrt{\lambda_2} \simeq 1.143 $. The minor axis of the ellipse is along  $ e_1 $, the eigenvector associated with the largest eigenvalue of G, where  $ \lambda_1 \simeq 5.241 $, giving  $ 1/\sqrt{\lambda_1} \simeq 0.437 $.

assets.label: Figure A5.6
assets.caption: Figure A5.6 Surfaces for a multivariate normal (MVN) distribution. Left: Surfaces of equal probability assuming that the additive-genetic values associated with the characters  $ z_1 $ and  $ z_2 $ in Example A5.1 are  $ \sim \mathrm{MVN}(\mu, \mathbf{G}) $. These surfaces are ellipses centered at  $ \mu $, with the major axis of the ellipse along  $ e_1 $ and the minor axis along  $ e_2 $, whose lengths (for a fixed c) are, respectively,  $ \sqrt{\lambda_1} = 2.289 $ and  $ \sqrt{\lambda_2} = 0.875 $. Right: A plot of the associated probability density. Slicing along either the major or minor axis gives a normal curve. Because the variance in the major axis is greater, the curve is much broader along this axis. The covariance between the breeding values of  $ z_1 $ and  $ z_2 $ rotates the distribution so that the principal axes ( $ e_1 $,  $ e_2 $) do not coincide with the original ( $ z_1 $,  $ z_2 $) axes.

prerequisites.why_needed: 本附录提供了向量变换、对称矩阵和规范轴等数学基础，这些直接用于第30章中多元选择分析（如γ矩阵和适应曲面）的推导与理解。
key_points: 对称矩阵的特征值和特征向量是第30章中γ矩阵的基础。
规范变换简化二次型，用于描述适应曲面的形状。
向量和矩阵的几何解释支持多元育种者方程的应用。
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前附录明确引用第30章关于Pearson-Lande-Arnold适应回归中的γ矩阵，并通过示例A5.1涉及多元育种者方程，这两者都是第30章的核心内容。
